chapter_title: Concerning the Dragon with Fourteen Heads; what it is and [...]
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a systematic microcosm teaching (body-anatomy ↔ fourteen heads ↔ five dens) in an impersonal, enumerative correspondential style (CORE). The opening Q&A and dialogue attributions are later compilation frame (MIXED where they wrap a substantive doctrinal question/answer). A clear pastoral/application drift occurs near the end: paragraph 7 applies the teaching to the believer’s struggle and introduces institutional identity language (“elect”), and the final paragraph is a disciple-response closure (FRAME).

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.251⟩
[ ... ] is distributed [ ... ] the laws of the Magi. They say that there is a dragon with fourteen heads, and it is gathered in and [ ... ] den with five refuges. [ ... ] What really is a corporeal dragon with fourteen heads? Or is it another spiritual lesson?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic/dialogue frame and audience-address formulas: “[Once again], one of his disciples asked the apostle…”, and “Now, I beseech you, my master, that you may instruct me…”. Kept the substantive doctrinal question about the fourteen-headed dragon and five refuges.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological/anthropological question is likely older teaching content, but it is embedded in a later Q&A wrapper (“Once again… disciple… apostle… I beseech you, my master”).

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.252⟩
There is never a dragon in the flesh with fourteen heads, as the Magi say! Rather, this is a spiritual lesson. It was uttered in virginity [ ... ] the Magi did not understand [ ... ] all their words that are written [ ... spiri]tual (?).
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: “Then the apostle says to him:”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching voice denies literalism and asserts a ‘spiritual lesson’—compatible with the core’s impersonal explanatory mode, but the polemical framing against “the Magi” and the meta-textual tone (“words that are written…”) may reflect Mani-era or later editorial contextualization; hence MIXED rather than pure CORE.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this is how this earth [ ... ] to it, as it is accounted a corporeal dragon [ ... ] I will instruct you [ ... ] the dragon is this doctrine [ ... ] of the flesh [ ... ] also the fourteen heads that are distributed over the dragon are these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal expository setup moving directly into definition and enumeration (“the fourteen heads… are these”)—a hallmark of the systematic substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The seven sense organs on the head of the body are the two of sight by which one sees; the two of sound by which one hears; the two of scent by which one smells; also the tongue [ ... ] by which one selects, receiving there the different tastes that occur in every form.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure correspondential-anatomical enumeration (sense faculties mapped as ‘heads’) staying within the system (body/faculty mapping), with no institutional or exhortative pivot.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the seven heads of the dragon, the seven sense organs that are on the upper part of the person; [ ... ] below. The seven of the torso are these: two [ ... ]; the two [ ... ] ruler [ ... ] the seven heads that are above; so with the ones below they total and make fourteen heads of the dragon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuing numbered/structural mapping and totaling logic (“they total and make fourteen”)—systematic teaching register characteristic of the core.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.253⟩
Conversely, the five dens about which they have spoken, where the dragon is congregated and protrudes, are these: the first is the tongue; the second is the lungs; the third is the heart; the fourth is the spleen; the fifth is the blood that dwells in them. Again, if it shall look out from them [and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by] its fourteen heads.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Another systematic set (five dens) mapped to internal organs, then described mechanistically (“it wages war by its fourteen heads”)—cosmos/body mechanics without pastoral address.

Application-voice paragraph: shifts from what the dragon *is* to what one must *do* (“struggles… is victorious… kills it”), and introduces institutional identity labels (“holy righteous one, elect, good person”) and eschatological reward language—typical late pastoral graft, consistent with the chapter’s second-half application drift signal.

paragraphs.core_text: So, behold, I have taught you of the dragon that exists with its fourteen heads and five dens, wherein it is concealed and hidden. It does through them [ ... / its des]ire all the time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Didactic recap that remains within the system (dragon/heads/dens/desire mechanics) without institutional prescriptions; reads like a core concluding summary rather than hagiographic closure.
Disciple-response and blessing formula (“Then that disciple says… My heart has been persuaded… Blessed is…”) functions as compilation frame/closure rather than substrate exposition.
